checks: The inverse bound and uniformly bounded affine slopes give uniform bounds for the bulk negative logarithm and its gradient. The support-plane distance from a fixed inball center has a uniform positive lower bound, which turns Gauss–Green for the radial field into a uniform surface mass bound.

The field uses g(R)=R^{-1}∫_0^R f(r)dr, with f vanishing near zero. It is continuously differentiable at zero and satisfies g+Rg'=f. At each fixed j the original affine minimum is positive and continuous, so the product field is Lipschitz and produces no interface measure across active-cell ties.

On positive rates the term differentiating the spatial test is bounded by sup_{t≥epsilon/lambda_j}t exp(−t) times the uniformly bounded inverse mass. The actual support of cell i gives −c_i·(X−o)=A_i(o); positivity of A_i(o) is supplied by the slice predecessor.

The signed identity with arbitrary smooth spatial tests yields the measure kernel by Fubini on the compact rate interval. The factor h/R is exactly the reciprocal-rate normalization. Restriction away from zero avoids any use of a zero-rate term.

Absolute continuity of the positive weighted sum excludes every positive atom of each positive cell component. Its decreasing tail is locally bounded by total radial log mass divided by r. The decreasing slice versions have finite one-sided limits near any strictly positive threshold because each weight is positive. Subtracting the two finite sums pays each new contribution by losses at the same spatial positions.

Source 1ec792c66c5ddc47 §§5,8 and d3b1d852e0e3ae4b §§2–4 give the exact kernel and compensation scope. The frozen proof derives its needed positive-rate identity directly, without a labeled allocation of the boundary or any unproved full rate-zero identity.
